blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — vincristine neurotoxicity monitoring
stem: A client receiving vincristine develops new paresthesias and decreased deep-tendon reflexes. Which nursing interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: These findings are consistent with vincristine neurotoxicity; perform a focused neurologic assessment because toxicity is dose related and may require treatment modification.
options.B: These findings indicate improving peripheral-nerve function and support continuing the same vincristine plan without additional neurologic assessment.
options.C: These findings are unlikely to be medication related because clinically important neuromuscular toxicity is not a recognized effect of vincristine therapy.
options.D: These findings primarily suggest cardiomyopathy, so cardiac imaging should replace neurologic assessment when vincristine-related toxicity is suspected.

rationale: Current vincristine labeling states that neurotoxicity is dose related and that sensory impairment and paresthesias may occur early, with continued treatment leading to motor difficulties and loss of deep-tendon reflexes. Neurologic evaluation is needed to detect toxicity and determine whether dosage modification is necessary. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize paresthesias and reduced reflexes as vincristine neurotoxicity and perform neurologic assessment to support timely treatment reassessment.
source_document_title: VINCRISTINE SULFATE injection — Full Prescribing Information
source_locator: Dosage and Administration: neurotoxicity appears dose related. Adverse Reactions—Neurologic: sensory impairment and paresthesia may occur first; continued treatment can cause motor difficulty, loss of deep-tendon reflexes, foot drop, ataxia, and paralysis.
source_claim_supported: Vincristine causes dose-related neurotoxicity including paresthesias and loss of deep-tendon reflexes and warrants neurologic reassessment.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: monitor for dose-limiting toxicity, recognize neurologic adverse effects, and report findings that may require treatment modification.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed absolute-word cues and balanced all options around competing toxicity interpretations.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current vincristine label; no residual cue or second answer remains.
